Chapter 8: The Return of Fear—Setbacks and Disillusionment
As the months rolled by, you could feel a shift in Egypt’s mood. Remember that electric sense of hope? Well, it started to fade, giving way to frustration—and for some, a creeping fear. The regime that once loomed over everyone was gone, but what filled the gap felt just as unstable.
Protests didn’t stop, but the atmosphere had changed. Now, when people took to the streets, they faced doubt, and sometimes, outright violence.
Imagine a young man who poured his heart into the revolution—he stood in the square, risking everything. Now, he looks around and feels lost. Political parties argue on TV, the military flexes its muscles, and those early promises of justice? They seem to vanish into thin air, replaced by new rules and new forms of repression. Even close friends, once shoulder-to-shoulder, now find themselves on opposite sides, arguing about what comes next.
The military, who once said they’d protect the revolution, started cracking down. Curfews popped up. Activists were taken away. And the media—remember how it was a force for change? Suddenly, it became a minefield. Some journalists pushed back, trying to keep leaders honest. Others slipped right back into silence, afraid to speak out.
Meanwhile, everyday people were stuck in the crossfire. Think of a mother who once celebrated the president’s fall. Now, she lies awake at night, worried for her kids. Prices are climbing, jobs are hard to find, and uncertainty hangs in the air. Was all that sacrifice really worth it? That question weighed on everyone’s mind.
You start to see—revolutions aren’t neat and tidy. The old systems that held Egypt together for decades? They didn’t just vanish. Those networks adapted, while the new leaders struggled to stand on their own. For so many, the dream of a brighter tomorrow felt like it was slipping further away.
Yet, even in the middle of all that disappointment, something powerful remained. Small acts of courage. Activists kept organizing, journalists asked the tough questions, and ordinary people refused to let go of hope.
The journey was tougher than anyone expected, but the revolutionary spirit—well, that was something not so easily extinguished.
